body:
## Problem

Every scheduler step walks the first running request's KV-cache block list in Python, counting blocks shared by all requests. With one request the walk covers the whole context: about 4,000 iterations per step at 64k tokens. Only cascade attention uses the result. It is off by default, and the V2 model runner ignores the value. Reported in #53683.

## Fix

Skip the walk when cascade attention is disabled.

## Effect

Scheduler CPU time, one request, block size 16, laptop CPU:

| context | decode step, before | after | whole chunked prefill, before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16k | 42.6 µs | 18.2 µs | 3.70 ms | 2.47 ms |
| 64k | 117.3 µs | 17.1 µs | 19.68 ms | 10.90 ms |

Batches of unrelated requests see no change.

End to end, RTX 4090, Qwen3-0.6B, one request, 512 output tokens, 6 rounds:

| async scheduling | prompt | median ITL, before | after | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| off | 64k | 10.71 ms | 10.60 ms | -1.0% |
| off | 128k | 18.63 ms | 18.38 ms | -1.3% |

With async scheduling on (the default) there is no measurable change, because the scheduler runs while the GPU is busy. vLLM turns async scheduling off for pooling models and several speculative decoding methods.

## Tests

Three new unit tests: cascade off skips the walk, cascade on keeps it, an empty queue gives zeros. Existing scheduler tests give the same results with and without this PR.

## Related

#53690 (open) stops the walk early for a single request. This PR also covers batches that share a prefix. The two do not conflict.
